sample_tweets.text: I've been made aware of a post from someone representing Rufus who says I'm very confused about this post. I've reported that Windows Defender went bananas after I installed Rufus on a Windows 11 device. It immediately popped up warnings about hacktools and trojans being installed while it was installing. I wish I had a record of it but I nuked everything after the alerts. https:// github.com/pbatard/rufus/issue s/3064
I mean, I might boost this post, but I'm sure as hell not going to like it. Am I weird or what?
why is liking your own comment even a thing?
Is it ironic that your Windoze PC gets infected while trying to download a file that allows you to write an installable Linux ISO? I think very much so and I'm still LOLing about it.
@ gunchleoc @ aetios @ jab01701mid Right, so you get the idea behind this post :)
I didn't realize how strong a community Rufus has. Please don't shoot the messenger.
I love all the commentary about how I'm supposedly inventing things here. Supply chain hacks or just selling one's site/brand happens. If you don't like the results too bad. Check them yourself.

Look, compromises happen to everyone. I have received a ton of private messages asking if I'm okay. But the reality is that I stopped using Windoze a long time ago and this was a kind of one-off thing where I was trying to re-image an old system anyway (away from Windoze).

A kind reader submitted the Rufus installer to any.run, a sandbox which walks through the installation of software to find malware that gets installed only *AFTER* the executable is clicked. You can see exactly all of the post-install prompts to download additional software that I also saw. https:// infosec.exchange/@jordinki/117 492425049116266
However, in my defense Google's default search results list rufus[.]ie as the authoritative site

No clue whether the resulting ISO is also malicious, but tried running it just for giggles on a spare Windows PC from bootup and the machine's bios said nope, wouldn't allow b/c security policy. Not sure if it's related but I've never seen that message before trying to boot up from a USB.

Not sure who needs to know this, but if you download and install the Windows version of Rufus, the free software for writing ISO images to USB/CD-ROM, your PC will end up with about 100 trojans. Edit: The site I downloaded from was rufus[.]ie which is apparently the official site. During installation, the software threw up a couple of rather verbose messages saying it needed to download additional components.

🚨🇺🇸 CIA contractor arrested for allegedly leaking top secret information to romantic partner Ian A. Brinksman, 42, of Washington, D.C., has been charged with unlawfully transmitting national defense information. ⠀ The Justice Department alleges Brinksman used his access as a CIA contractor to retrieve five classified intelligence reports outside the scope of his work. 🚨🇫🇷 Quad9 to withdraw DNS services from France after court ruling Quad9 says it will stop serving users in France on November 24 after a French court ordered the nonprofit DNS provider to block domains accused of streaming pirated sports broadcasts. ⠀ The case was brought by sports broadcaster beIN, which argued that the domains infringed its audiovisual rights. The court reduced Quad9’s potential penalty from €580,000 to €1,000 per day but upheld the blocking requirement. ⠀ Quad9 says it cannot reliably identify French users without collecting location data, while blocking the domains globally would apply French law to users in every country. The organization has chosen to withdraw from France instead of altering its DNS responses. An appeal is pending. 🚨🇺🇸 Railway says breach potentially exposed secrets in around 100,000 workspaces Cloud development platform Railway says an attacker gained access to internal systems and potentially exposed encrypted environment variables belonging to up to 1.85% of its workspaces, or roughly 100,000. ⠀ Some variables were decrypted using compromised credentials. These may have contained API keys, database credentials, private registry credentials and other sensitive information. Railway believes the attacker was searching for AI provider API keys to conduct model distillation attacks. ⠀ The attack occurred between October 20 and October 22. Railway temporarily stopped new builds and deployments while responding, although existing customer applications remained online. Railway says individual user accounts were not accessed, but it has not ruled out possible access to source code while its investigation continues. ⠀ All customers who stored credentials on Railway before October 21 should rotate them and review connected services for suspicious activity. Railway has also invalidated access tokens, rotated internal credentials and worked with providers including GitHub, GitLab, OpenAI, Anthropic and Stripe to revoke potentially exposed keys. Source: https:// blog.railway.com/p/preliminary -report-october-security-incident

🚨🇺🇸 GoDaddy revokes hundreds of thousands of SSL certificates after policy errors GoDaddy has completed a mass revocation involving 403,643 SSL/TLS certificates issued under its GoDaddy and Starfield certificate chains. ⠀ The certificates contained policy information that did not match the company’s published Certificate Policy and Certification Practice Statement. The discrepancies involved certificate policy identifiers and links referencing the certificate authority’s documented practices. ⠀ GoDaddy initially identified 404,607 affected certificates but later corrected the total to 403,643. By October 22: • 378,067 certificates had been revoked • 25,576 had already expired • No affected certificates remained valid ⠀ GoDaddy missed the original five-day revocation deadline while coordinating replacements with affected customers, including government, financial and healthcare organizations. The incident was a compliance failure, not a confirmed security breach or private key compromise. Customers still using an affected certificate may see browser security warnings or have their website become inaccessible until the replacement certificate is installed.

🚨 Ruby fixes three regex engine bugs linked to remote code execution risks Ruby has released versions 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 to address three memory corruption bugs in its Onigmo regular expression engine. ⠀ The flaws involve a double free and two integer overflow conditions. GitLab found that specially crafted regex patterns could trigger the bugs and potentially allow remote code execution. Four GitLab vulnerabilities rely on the underlying issues: • CVE-2026-89078 • CVE-2026-93577 • CVE-2026-97229 • CVE-2026-110264 ⠀ Applications are only exposed when they compile regular expressions from attacker-controlled input. Ruby warns that Regexp.timeout and pattern length limits do not reliably prevent exploitation. Administrators should update to Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13 and avoid compiling untrusted regex patterns if an immediate upgrade is not possible.

🚨 Critical Okta Access Gateway flaw allows administrators to execute system commands; CVE-2026-115547 The vulnerability affects the Okta Access Gateway Admin Console and carries a CVSS score of 9.1. ⠀ An authenticated administrator can submit specially formatted configuration values to execute commands within the context of the OAG service account. Key details: • Network exploitable • Low attack complexity • Administrative access required • No user interaction required • Affects OAG versions before 2026.10.2 ⠀ Okta has resolved the vulnerability in Access Gateway 2026.10.2. Administrators should manually upgrade affected appliances. Source: https:// trust.okta.com/security-adviso ries/command-execution-via-admin-console-input-in-okta-access-gateway-cve-2026-115547

🚨 PHP warns of another unpatched remote code execution risk; CVE-2026-115560 The newly disclosed vulnerability is separate from the two PHP2Shell flaws patched earlier this week and is not fixed by PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. ⠀ PHP says exploitation requires an unusual configuration where an application: • Uses php_binary or php_serialize as its session serializer • Changes the serializer to php at runtime before session_start() • Has session upload progress enabled ⠀ PHP considers the risk unlikely and plans to release a fix during its next regular update cycle. Until then, administrators with affected configurations should set: session.upload_progress.enabled=0 Applications that do not change the session serializer at runtime are not exposed through this path. No exploitation has been reported. Source: https://www. php.net/

🚨 Palo Alto Networks warns PAN-OS is affected by PHP2Shell remote code execution flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 affect the PAN-OS management web interface, including the HTTPS interface and XML API service. ⠀ Affected products include: • PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 release trains • All Panorama versions • All WildFire WF-500 and WF-500-B appliances ⠀ No special configuration is required, but the risk is highest when the management interface is exposed to the internet. Palo Alto Networks rates the product impact at CVSS 8.7. PAN-OS hotfixes are expected between October 26 and 30, while dates for Panorama and WildFire appliance fixes remain unconfirmed. The company is not aware of malicious exploitation targeting its products. GlobalProtect and Captive Portal are not affected. Source: https:// security.paloaltonetworks.com/ CVE-2026-109618
